dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract

evidence.note: Read the entire JAX source tree and supporting files (pikachu/mewtwo/venusaur_jax, pokedex_config, pokeball, lora, types, benchmark, smoke_jax) in full, deliberately scrolling to capture cut-off embed_prefix/embed_suffix — a thorough map of the full forward/sample flow, not a skim.

Ran smoke_jax to confirm JAX behavior, then wrote a dedicated inspection script to extract exact pokedex parameter shapes; step 21 records precise config and tensor layouts (conv kernel [16,16,3,32], 2x2 patches, sincos2d pos embedding, encoderblock scan) — deriving exact shapes/conventions from the source.
Pre-implementation notes on mirroring JAX RoPE exactly and transposing einsum kernels to use Linear layers — anticipating weight-layout parity pitfalls.

When sample parity was slightly off, revisited Flax semantics and discovered nn.gelu defaults to tanh approximation, then investigated TF32 matmul/cudnn precision — resolving numerical-convention discrepancies against the JAX source as they surfaced.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the full JAX source and config, enumerated the required API surface (verified via imports at step 58), and derived exact tensor shapes and parameter layouts via an inspection script (matching the level-5/8 anchors). It went further by tracing weight transposition and RoPE, anticipating layout pitfalls, and revisiting Flax/precision semantics (gelu tanh, TF32) to resolve parity discrepancies as they arose — the self-correcting, evidence-backed behavior of the 8-10 band. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because RNG/noise-ordering conventions were handled more reactively than pre-derived, placing it at 9.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones

evidence.note: Wrote model.py then immediately copied to model_optimized.py and benchmarked before parity was established — a slight blur of the checkpoint gate, though occurring during the correctness-fixing phase.

Iterated on model.py to fix parity (GELU tanh, TF32), re-copying each time; at step 30 correctness PASSES, baseline recorded, and optimization phase explicitly begins — phase gate respected and model.py frozen thereafter.

Optimization treated as discrete numbered experiments, each recorded to results.tsv with improvement_pct and PASS/FAIL as an explicit done-signal; step 36 sketches upcoming experiments 2-5, showing some forward planning.
Reverted the unproductive torch.compile experiment and counted experiments against the ≤8 budget, showing bounded discrete-experiment discipline.
Final milestone verification: confirmed both model.py and model_optimized.py pass, shim exports from optimized, and imports resolve — checkable end-state for each artifact.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced implement→parity→freeze checkpoint→bounded optimization, kept the correctness checkpoint frozen after parity, pointed the shim at the optimized file, and ran optimization as discrete experiments each with a PASS/FAIL improvement_pct done-signal recorded in results.tsv — squarely above the level-5 anchor and into level-8 territory. It falls short of 10 because experiments were chosen incrementally rather than planned upfront as a risk-ordered, hypothesis-driven search of the full ≤8 budget, and there was a minor checkpoint-before-parity blur at step 23. This places the observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks

evidence.note: Ran smoke_jax.py to confirm JAX reference and inspected pokedex parameter shapes for correctness of the port, but did not author any independent numerical parity comparison; relied on the provided harness.

Diagnosed parity failures surfaced by benchmark.py (sample check 0.0012 vs 0.0005 tol), fixed GELU tanh approximation and TF32 precision, reasoning explicitly about atol/rtol — engaging with the JAX-referenced comparison rather than building its own.

After each of ~8 optimizations re-ran benchmark.py and recorded status=PASS alongside latency in results.tsv, confirming output equivalence (not just the latency number) each time — but exclusively through the provided harness.

Final verification re-ran benchmark.py and checked both model.py and model_optimized.py imports/PASS; no self-built per-method or layer-level parity checks or seeded-determinism harness ever constructed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent used benchmark.py's JAX-referenced loss/sample parity plus latency PASS/FAIL for the main forward/sample paths and disciplinedly re-checked PASS after every optimization — squarely anchor 5. It engaged thoughtfully with numerical divergences (GELU, TF32, tolerance semantics), but it never built its own per-method (embed_prefix/embed_suffix/forward/sample_actions) parity checks, seeded-determinism verification, or guards independent of the supplied harness, which anchor 8 requires. Hence a solid 5.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget

evidence.note: After each optimization the agent appends a live results.tsv row with baseline_ms, latency_ms, improvement_pct, PASS status, and a short description of the change — a running ledger updated per experiment tying each attempt to its result and parity status.

Analysis consistently identifies the incumbent fastest-passing variant and flags marginal/noise results (e.g. 'Roughly the same 33.1 vs 32.957 - marginal noise', '28.59ms better') without re-deriving, showing it tracks which variant currently wins.

Detected torch.compile as unproductive (slower, 30.15 vs 29.69) and reverted from a saved backup (exp6_backup.py) — recognizing an unproductive thread and not shipping a worse variant; also kept exp1_backup.py.

Near the end explicitly reconciles budget: 'We've used about 7 experiments', then enumerates all 10 results entries vs 8 'actual optimization experiments', and writes autoresearch_logs.md. Budget counting is slightly fuzzy (whether reverts count) and the logs.md was batch-written at the end rather than continuously.
Final verification re-runs benchmark and confirms both model.py and model_optimized.py pass, restating the fastest passing latency (28.48ms/39%) and budget accounting before submitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an accurate running ledger in results.tsv, logging latency, parity status, and a hypothesis-like description for each experiment, and it consistently knew the current fastest-passing variant and reverted unproductive threads (torch.compile) rather than shipping them — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the autoresearch_logs.md trail was written retroactively near the end rather than used continuously as a live decision instrument, and its budget accounting (8 vs 10 entries, whether reverts count) was somewhat muddled. It clearly exceeds level 5, which it fully satisfies (both trail files, per-experiment status, known best, tracked remaining budget).

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations

evidence.note: Sample-parity failure (0.0012 vs 0.0005 tol) diagnosed to root cause: Flax nn.gelu defaults to tanh approximation; applied targeted fix to both vit and mewtwo blocks rather than random tweaks.
Residual numerical gap pursued further to root causes — TF32/cudnn precision settings and a from __future__ import-ordering bug — until parity PASSED. Principled, not flailing.
torch.compile regressed latency (30.15 vs 29.69ms); agent reverted cleanly from a saved backup (exp6_backup.py) instead of keeping the slower variant.
SDPA-in-mewtwo flagged as a precision risk (custom big_neg + fp32 softmax) and validated within tolerance before adopting — treating optimization as a correctness risk.
Recognized marginal results (33.1 vs 32.9; 29.67 vs 29.69) as noise and redirected to bigger wins (SDPA, inlined suffix), ending on the fastest passing implementation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed parity failures to their root causes — GELU tanh approximation, dtype/TF32 precision, import ordering — and made targeted corrections rather than pressing on or tweaking randomly, matching anchor 8. It abandoned an unproductive optimization (torch.compile) and reverted cleanly using saved backups, and ended keeping the fastest passing variant. It stops short of 10 because the optimization phase leaned on try-and-measure with some noise-level results accepted, rather than a fully systematic failure-driven budget redirection.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline

evidence.note: After correctness PASS, enumerates a ranked list of optimization hypotheses (SDPA, reduced kernel launches, cached embeddings) before touching model_optimized.py — deliberate budget planning.

Sequence of distinct, hypothesis-driven experiments each logged to results.tsv with latency/improvement: fused QKV+SDPA, avoid double preprocess, batched vision, SDPA in mewtwo, optimized sample loop — biggest structural wins attempted first.
Tries torch.compile, measures it as slower, reverts cleanly — abandons an unproductive path rather than pressing on.
'precomputed buffers' and 'kv_cache as list' produced noise-level results (33.1 vs 32.96; 29.67 vs 29.69) — mildly redundant experiments that prevent a top score.

Explicitly counts experiments against the ≤8 cap and lists all of them, keeping fastest passing impl; but rationalizes '8 successful + 2 reverted' when ~9 model-changing trials ran — slight stretching of the cap.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treated the budget as scarce: it pre-listed hypotheses, ran genuinely distinct experiments sequenced from highest expected payoff, logged each to results.tsv, abandoned torch.compile when it failed to help, and stopped keeping the fastest passing implementation — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because two experiments produced noise-level redundant results and it loosely rationalized the experiment count ('8 successful + 2 reverted') rather than strictly bounding to 8.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, two-phase engineering task: first faithfully port an under-documented renamed JAX policy to PyTorch behind a precise API contract (many named symbols/methods, deterministic behavior, numerical parity), then produce an optimized inference variant that preserves outputs while beating a latency gate. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering JAX semantics for exact parity, a rigid interface surface, a hard budget (≤8 optimization experiments, keep fastest passing), and required experiment bookkeeping. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation and verification, sequences correctness-before-speed strictly, and manages the experiment budget deliberately.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract
dimensions.description: Reading and understanding the existing JAX policy, its config, and the exact required PyTorch API surface before and while writing code.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Numerical parity and topology compatibility are impossible without precisely understanding the JAX implementation's layer shapes, init, flow (embed_prefix/suffix, sampling loop), and the specified symbol/method contract; acting blind guarantees rework.

anchors.0: Starts writing model.py without reading the JAX source or the config; invents an architecture.
anchors.3: Skims the JAX file and copies obvious layers, but never maps out the full forward/sample flow or the required symbol list, missing methods or misreading shapes.
anchors.5: Reads the JAX policy and config, enumerates the required symbols/methods (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard, embed_prefix/suffix, sample_actions, PokemonCenter.img/llm), and understands the main data flow before coding.
anchors.8: Systematically traces each JAX module to its intended PyTorch equivalent — parameter layouts, init, dtype/device handling, the noise/time/timestep semantics and sampling loop — and records assumptions about ambiguous points, distinguishing the actual JAX contract from any public-project prior.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed mental model of the entire policy: derives exact tensor shapes and numerical conventions (weight transposition, normalization, RNG/noise ordering) from the JAX source, anticipates parity pitfalls (e.g. layout differences, default configs), and revisits the source to resolve discrepancies as they surface during implementation.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — build each API piece, achieve parity, freeze model.py, then run bounded optimization experiments — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task has an explicit phase gate (correct model.py must be preserved as checkpoint before optimizing a copy) and a scoring split across topology/parity/latency; treating it as one push risks optimizing before correctness or corrupting the checkpoint.

anchors.0: No structure; edits everything at once, mixes optimization into model.py, no notion of phase gate.
anchors.3: Vague two-step intent but no explicit milestones or done-criteria; may begin optimizing before parity is established.
anchors.5: Clear phases: implement full API, verify parity, copy to model_optimized.py, then optimize — with the correctness checkpoint respected and the shim pointed at the optimized file.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and independently checkable (per-method parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, checkpoint frozen, each optimization experiment scoped), with optimization treated as a bounded sequence of discrete experiments rather than open-ended tinkering.
anchors.10: A disciplined milestone hierarchy that orders by risk (hardest-to-parity components first), defines the exact done-signal for each, protects the frozen checkpoint, and plans the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search (what hypothesis each tests) before spending the budget.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks for topology, layer-level numerical parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and using the benchmark harness to confirm latency gains and preserved outputs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The submission is scored precisely on these parities and the latency gate; without self-built numerical comparisons against the JAX reference and disciplined use of benchmark.py, the agent cannot know it succeeded and optimizations may silently change outputs.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes port is correct and that optimizations preserve outputs without checking.
anchors.3: Runs the model once to see it doesn't crash, or runs benchmark.py only for latency, with no numerical comparison to the JAX reference.
anchors.5: Compares PyTorch outputs against the JAX reference for the main forward/sample paths and uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after optimization.
anchors.8: Builds layer-level / per-method parity checks (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, forward, sample_actions) with explicit tolerances, verifies determinism given fixed noise/time, and after every optimization re-checks output equivalence against the frozen model.py — not just the latency number.
anchors.10: A rigorous verification harness: systematic numerical comparison across components and end-to-end (loss and sampling) with sensible tolerances and seeded RNG, guards that catch subtle divergence introduced by each optimization, and cross-checks that benchmark.py's PASS status reflects true output parity rather than being gamed — verification designed before results are trusted.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which API pieces pass parity, which experiments have run against the ≤8 budget, and which is the current fastest passing implementation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard experiment cap, a required experiment trail (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md), and a 'keep the fastest passing' rule, losing track of what's done, what passed, and what's best leads to wasted budget or shipping a worse variant.

anchors.0: No tracking; doesn't know how many experiments have run, which passed, or which is fastest; trail files empty or absent.
anchors.3: Sparse notes; loses count of experiments or forgets which variant currently wins; trail is an afterthought.
anchors.5: Maintains results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/status per experiment and knows the current best passing variant and remaining budget.
anchors.8: Keeps an accurate running ledger tying each experiment to its hypothesis, latency, parity status, and budget consumed; consistently identifies the incumbent fastest-passing implementation and remaining parity gaps without re-deriving them.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining across both phases: detects when an optimization thread is unproductive early, avoids re-running equivalent experiments, and uses the trail as a live decision instrument to allocate the last few budget slots to the highest-value ideas.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations
dimensions.description: Revising approach when numerical parity fails, when an optimization breaks outputs, or when a latency experiment fails to improve — rather than pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Porting will surface parity mismatches and optimizations that regress correctness or don't help; with a capped budget, the agent must diagnose root causes and change course instead of burning experiments on a falsified approach.

anchors.0: Ignores failing parity or FAIL status; keeps the broken variant or barrels ahead on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Notices failures but responds with random tweaks rather than diagnosis; may keep a non-passing variant or abandon parity.
anchors.5: When parity or a benchmark fails, investigates the cause and adjusts (fixes layout/init, reverts a bad optimization, discards non-passing variants to keep the fastest passing one).
anchors.8: Diagnoses divergence to its root (e.g. a specific layer's numerics, RNG ordering, dtype) and makes targeted corrections; abandons unpromising optimization directions quickly to conserve budget and reverts cleanly to the frozen checkpoint when needed.
anchors.10: Treats each failure as evidence that updates the plan: isolates root causes systematically, redirects the remaining experiment budget toward hypotheses the failures point to, and ends with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing implementation rather than the last thing tried.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline
dimensions.description: Treating the ≤8 optimization experiments as a scarce resource allocated across distinct, hypothesis-driven attempts, and honoring the stop condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly caps experiments and requires stopping with the fastest passing implementation; undisciplined trial-and-error either exhausts the budget prematurely or overruns it, and is a meta-work demand beyond generic monitoring.

anchors.0: Ignores the cap entirely — either endless tinkering or no real optimization attempts, no notion of a stop rule.
anchors.3: Runs optimizations ad hoc with little differentiation between attempts and loose regard for the 8-experiment limit.
anchors.5: Stays within the budget, keeps distinct experiments, and stops with a passing implementation selected as fastest.
anchors.8: Allocates the budget deliberately across genuinely different optimization hypotheses, sequences them from highest expected payoff, and stops cleanly once diminishing returns or the cap is reached.
anchors.10: Runs a near-optimal search under the constraint: each experiment tests a distinct, well-motivated idea informed by prior results, redundant attempts are avoided, and the final choice is justified as the best latency-vs-parity trade-off within the spent budget.
